response.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb, AVG(APTT - PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM Laboratory WHERE UA >= 3.9 GROUP BY ID) SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS avg_hgb, AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM per_patient;

assumptions.assumption: The UA threshold is inclusive (UA >= 3.9), and UA is in the same units as the stored values.

APTT minus PT is computed per record, so a record missing either APTT or PT contributes nothing to that patient's average. Ignoring missing values at every step means NULLs are dropped by AVG at each level.
Patients with no qualifying records, or with no non-null HGB or APTT-PT values, are excluded from the outer average, since their per-patient value is NULL.
The 'across all patients' averages are unweighted means of the per-patient averages, not record-level means.

alternatives.interpretation: Compute each patient's APTT-PT as the average APTT minus the average PT over the qualifying records, rather than averaging per-record differences. This differs only when APTT and PT have different missing-value patterns.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb, AVG(APTT) - AVG(PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM Laboratory WHERE UA >= 3.9 GROUP BY ID) SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS avg_hgb, AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM per_patient;
